summary: On certain enchanted items, the Anvil will display a "too expensive" message before attempting to repair, combine, or rename them
description:
Putting certain enchanted items into the first anvil slot and doing nothing else will show "too expensive", even though trying to rename or combine with a book will still be allowed.

What I expected to happen was:

If I put any item into the Anvil slot without doing anything it would just show me the crossed out arrow.

What actually happened was:

I put an item with multiple enchantments and it showed me it was "too expensive to do nothing with it"

Steps to reproduce:

1. Enchant a diamond sword with these enchants:

Fire Aspect II

Looting III

Sharpness V

Unbreaking III

Knockback II

Sweeping Edge III

2. Put a normal diamond sword in the first anvil slot, notice it will just show the crossed out arrow.

3. Put the enchanted sword into the first anvil slot, it will show "too expensive".

4. Try to rename it or combine books with that sword, it will then show the actual enchantment cost.

Edit: In newer versions renaming the item might be required but the bug is still there.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Singleplayer Survival world with default settings.
3. Obtain an anvil.
4. Enchant a diamond sword with Fire Aspect II, Looting III, Sharpness V, Unbreaking III, Knockback II, and Sweeping Edge III.
5. Open the anvil and put a normal diamond sword into the first slot.
6. Observe that the anvil shows only the crossed-out arrow.
7. Replace the normal diamond sword with the enchanted diamond sword in the first slot.
8. Observe that the anvil shows “Too Expensive!” without any repair, combination, or renaming being attempted.
9. Try to rename the enchanted sword or combine it with an enchanted book.
10. Observe that the anvil shows the actual enchantment cost instead of “Too Expensive!”.
Observed Behavior:
When the enchanted diamond sword is placed in the anvil’s first (target) slot with the second slot empty and no rename is entered, the anvil displays **“Too Expensive!”** instead of only showing the disabled output arrow. No repair, combination, or rename operation has been selected, so there is no actual operation whose cost should be evaluated.

For comparison, placing an otherwise identical unenchanted diamond sword in the first slot displays only the crossed-out output arrow. Despite the premature **“Too Expensive!”** message, entering a new name or placing a compatible enchanted book in the second slot causes the anvil to recalculate the operation and display the corresponding enchantment or rename cost. In versions where a rename is required to trigger the calculation, the same erroneous message is still shown before that operation is selected.
Expected Behavior: Putting an item, including one with multiple enchantments, into the first anvil slot without a second item or rename should only display the crossed-out arrow, rather than “Too Expensive!”. The anvil should calculate and display a cost only after a valid repair, combination, or renaming operation is selected, and the enchanted sword should remain usable for such operations when their actual cost is within the allowed limit.
